# External data index

## 2026-09-01 (later) — CORRECTION and the real state of the surface-data gap

**Correction to this file:** the `pinfin_chf_water_fc72.csv` row below was documented as 190 rows. It actually has **175**. Corrected in the table.

**More important correction — the gap is not closed.** An earlier note in this file implied the engineered-surface data situation was merely "thin." A column-level audit on 2026-09-01 found something structural: **no file in this repository has both an operating condition (mass flux) and a surface characteristic (roughness or contact angle) in the same row.**

| Family | Rows | Mass flux | Pressure | Contact angle | Roughness |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LUT (`data/chf_long_clean.csv`) | 11,592 | yes | yes | — | — |
| NRC (`data/nrc_chf_clean.csv`) | 24,443 | yes | yes | — | — |
| KAERI + Zhao + Hardik/Prabhu | ~2,900 | yes | yes | — | — |
| `pinfin_chf_water_fc72.csv` | 175 | — | — | **—** | yes |
| `ali2018_fecral_atf_pool_boiling_chf.csv` | 4 | — | yes | yes (1 of 4) | yes |
| `zhang2023_boiling_crisis_sapphire_surfaces_chf.csv` | 6 | — | yes | yes | — |
| `son2020_cr_cral_surface_roughness_dryout_kinetics.csv` | 16 | — | — | yes | yes (but **no CHF**) |
| `ramakrishnan2026_copper_microchannel_ageing_chf.csv` | 10 | yes | — | aggregate only | aggregate only |

The two families cannot be unioned — pool vs. flow boiling is different physics, and a join produces a block-missing matrix (28,000 rows with NaN for every surface feature, ~200 with NaN for flow). Note also that the largest surface dataset, pin-fin, has **no contact-angle column at all**, though the outline names contact angle explicitly in §6.4 and in the §15 SHAP ranking.

**What closes it:** re-extracting the 14 source studies behind the Serrao et al. 2025 database — see `docs/references/TO_DOWNLOAD_surface_chf_papers.md` for the worklist, DOIs, per-paper yields, and the range-based validation method.

Remaining: Fong 2001, He & Chen 2023, Jo 2019, Cheol Lee 2019, Seo 2015 (22 points), plus figure digitisation for Kim 2019 / Son 2019 / Son 2020 / Kam 2015 Cr rows.

Every extraction was validated against Serrao et al. 2025's independently published min–max ranges before being trusted. Seven of eight matched exactly; the one that did not (Kam 2015) is flagged in the worklist rather than silently reconciled.

## 2026-09-01 update — 5 engineered-surface papers extracted (partial progress on the surface-data gap)

Five ScienceDirect PDFs the user downloaded (advisor-relevant, surface-characteristic CHF literature) were read and mined for data. All extraction was done from `pdftotext -layout` output (exact text, not eyeballed from rendered pages) and cross-checked internally where possible (see the Serrao/Ali cross-check below). Two are genuine point-level datasets that directly match the `paper_outline.docx` engineered-surface goal; three are source-list summaries (real per-study metadata/ranges, not raw points) — same "menu, not meal" caveat as the other summary files in this folder.

Source: A.F. Ali et al., *Nucl. Eng. Des.* 338 (2018) 218–231. | Small (n=4) but exact and directly on-topic — real engineered-surface CHF data, same physical configuration family (pool boiling) as `pinfin_chf_water_fc72.csv`. |
| `zhang2023_boiling_crisis_sapphire_surfaces_chf.csv` | Point-level, real | 6 | Pool-boiling CHF for six coatings on a sapphire heater (Cr, alumina, ITO, ZnO nanowires, CuO nanoleaves, SiO2 nanoparticles), each with a static contact angle. Source: L. Zhang et al., "A unifying criterion of the boiling crisis," *Nat. ## 2026-08-31 (later same day) update — the real NRC/OECD database was found

Correction to an earlier claim in this file and in the publication-readiness audit: the ~24,579-point NRC CHF database is **not actually gated behind OECD/NEA benchmark registration for the raw numbers**. A teammate located and transcribed it from a public NRC ADAMS document (`docs/references/ML22264A009.pdf`, accession ML22264A009, 457 pages, no paywall or membership required). What *is* still NEA-gated is the officially-distributed, benchmark-ready CSV version used by the formal AI/ML CHF benchmark exercise — but the underlying numbers were public all along, in an NRC public record, once someone did the transcription work. That work is now done. See `nrc_groeneveld_24579pt_chf_database.csv` below.


Everything in this folder is candidate data for the engineered-surface / multi-source phase described in `docs/manuscript/paper_outline.docx`. Two kinds of file live here and it matters which is which:

- **Point-level data** — real rows you can train/test/validate on.
- **Source-list summaries** — a list of *where* more data could come from (paper name, sample size, parameter ranges), with no actual data points. These are menus, not meals; do not mistake a large row count in one of these for usable data.

Do not treat the row counts here as usable data points; treat this as 30 real experiments waiting to be reduced to ~30 real (P, G, X, CHF)-type rows. |

## Why the full ~25,000-point NRC/OECD-NEA CHF database isn't just sitting here

It's a compilation of ~70 separate historical experiments (see `table4-2` above), several from the 1950s–1990s, not a single publicly downloadable file. The clean, ready-to-use version used by papers like Wang et al. (2026) is typically distributed only to teams registered for the formal OECD/NEA AI/ML CHF Benchmark (spec document: `docs/references/Benchmark on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning...Phase 1...pdf`). Getting more of it requires either (a) registering for that benchmark, or (b) manually transcribing more named sources from `ML19029B306.pdf` using the target list above.
